title: Unramified morphisms are formally unramified
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be an unramified morphism of schemes [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then $f$ is formally unramified [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism]. More precisely, for every first order thickening $T\subset T'$ over $S$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], affine or not, with closed immersion $i:T\to T'$ and structure morphism $b:T'\to S$, and any two morphisms $a'_1,a'_2:T'\to X$ with $f\circ a'_1=f\circ a'_2=b$ and $a'_1\circ i=a'_2\circ i$, one has $a'_1=a'_2$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02HE (lemma-unramified-formally-unramified), (1) implies (2); the non-affine form is Lemma 04F1 (lemma-formally-unramified-not-affine)
